criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli drain` (and the athena-core tests). A test through the drain over RealSteps and Athena::go shows the in-flight row's worktree equals the producer's live work tree (<state>/jobs/<id>/work, the path producer.rs uses), not <state>/kept/<id>/work.
criteria.evidence: `in_flight_row_names_the_producers_live_work_tree` (tests/drain.rs) runs drain::drain over RealSteps, which now calls Athena::go_with_stages. While the producer agent runs, the test reads the table and asserts four things: the row's worktree == root/jobs/<id>/work, it equals spec.workdir, the directory exists, and it is not under root/kept. producer.rs now builds its work tree from the same StateDir::work_dir helper that TableSink uses. I ran it and it passed, along with all 106 drain integration tests. The athena-core state tests (8, including the_live_work_tree_is_under_the_job_directory_and_not_the_kept_one) also passed.

criteria.criterion: A test through the real entry point forces a producer send-back after a failed self-check, and another after a verifier send-back. It shows the row's stage goes checks (or verifier) back to producer, and the row reads producer during the second producer invocation. Run with `cargo test`.
criteria.evidence: Two tests cover this, and both passed. `in_flight_row_goes_producer_checks_verifier_and_is_producer_again_after_a_self_check_send_back`: an unmet-criterion report causes a send-back, and the looks taken are exactly [producer, producer, checks, verifier], with the same worktree both times. `in_flight_row_moves_from_verifier_back_to_producer_when_the_rejected_job_is_retried`: a rejecting verdict, then a retry. The row goes producer → checks → verifier (first job), is moved to the retry job, and reads producer at the second producer invocation, with the retry's jobs/<id>/work. There is one row throughout. The core-level lifecycle test `stage_report_names_the_producer_again_after_a_send_back_then_checks_then_the_verifier` also passed.

findings.summary: A moved row carries a stage the retry job has not reached. After a rejection, the old job's row stays at 'verifier' even though the job has finished. When it moves to the retry job it keeps 'verifier' until that job's producer starts, so it spans the reading, the disk checks and the snapshot.
findings.evidence: InFlight::move_row keeps `stage`, and RealSteps::read calls it for ReadOf::Retry. The test in_flight_row_moves_from_verifier_back_to_producer_when_the_rejected_job_is_retried asserts dispatched[1] == [(retry_job, Stage::Verifier)]. If the process crashes in that window, it leaves a row saying a job that never ran its verifier was at the verifier. Later recovery (build job 9) has to interpret that. A simpler, more accurate rule would be to set the stage to producer when the row moves, or to remove the old row and let the retry's producer write a fresh one. This is documented behavior and acts on nothing now, so it is minor.

findings.summary: The criterion cites 'sections 7 and 11' of async-drain.md, but the build-jobs list is section 12. The candidate edited sections 7 and 12, which is correct.
findings.evidence: Headings in docs/design/async-drain.md: '## 11. Config block (proposed)' and '## 12. Ordered build jobs'. The 'Implemented (D145)' note is in section 12.

summary: The change passes: all 8 acceptance criteria are met, with no blocker or major finding. It adds the in-flight table as a single `in-flight.json` file in the state directory. Stages now come from the run itself: `Athena::go_with_stages` reports each stage at the points where the run enters the producer (every pass, so a send-back reports producer again), the checks, the verifier and a blocked job's landing, and the drain's own landing step reports landing too. No stage is guessed from display text. The worktree comes from a new shared helper, `StateDir::work_dir` (`jobs/<id>/work`), which producer.rs now uses too, so the table names the producer's live work tree rather than the kept copy of a timed-out job. Commands I ran, all passing: the 106 drain integration tests, the 29 drain unit tests, the lifecycle stage-report test and the athena-core state tests. Through the real drain and `RealSteps`, they show four things. The row's worktree equals the producer's working directory. A self-check send-back gives producer, producer, checks, verifier. A verifier rejection moves the row to the retry job, which reads producer at its second producer start. Leftover, missing and corrupt files are handled as specified. Existing tests are unchanged apart from one import line. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy (-D warnings) and full test runs passed. CHANGELOG.md and the design doc match the behavior, the config and workflow files are untouched, and every changed file is on the deliverables list. One minor design point: after a verifier rejection, the row moved to the retry job keeps the 'verifier' stage until that job's producer starts. Setting it to producer when it moves would be more accurate for later crash recovery.
